_comment: Importable Orcabot dashboard template. Unlike the other benchmark templates this one needs no orchestrator, no agent and no API key: the terminal's boot command runs the whole benchmark and serves its report on localhost, and the browser block is pointed at that server. Seed with bin/seed-benchmark-templates.
name: TTS Benchmark Runner
description: Run the open-weight TTS benchmark and read its report

items.content:
{"name": "TTS benchmark", "agentic": false, "bootCommand": "PORT=8099 # talkito refuses to fetch model weights when it cannot ask a human. The picker # below is interactive, but the download prompt would land in the middle of a # sweep the reader has walked away from, so it is answered in advance. export TALKITO_AUTO_APPROVE_DOWNLOADS=1 ROOT=/workspace/talkito BENCH=$ROOT/benchmark SERVE=/workspace/tts-report echo "== Orcabot: talkito TTS benchmark ==" # Serve a placeholder first, so the browser block has something at a stable URL from # the first second rather than an error until the run finishes. mkdir -p "$SERVE" [ -f "$SERVE/index.html" ] || printf '%s' 'TTS benchmark

Waiting for a run...

Pick engines in the terminal. This page reloads every 10 seconds and the report replaces it when the run finishes.

' > "$SERVE/index.html" curl -sf -o /dev/null --max-time 2 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" || ( cd "$SERVE" && nohup python3 -m http.server "$PORT" >/workspace/.tts-serve.log 2>&1 & ) # talkito's .gitmodules uses git@github.com: URLs and the sandbox has no SSH key, # so --recurse-submodules fails; both repos are cloned over HTTPS instead. # The harness ships inside talkito-benchmark, so tests-repo is not needed -- but # tools/paths.py still wants a talkito CHECKOUT (it looks for talkito/tts.py, not # the installed package), and benchmark/ inside talkito/ is the layout it resolves. [ -d "$ROOT/.git" ] || git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/robdmac/talkito.git "$ROOT" [ -d "$BENCH/.git" ] || git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/robdmac/talkito-benchmark.git "$BENCH" # piper needs no torch at all, and faster-whisper scores on CPU through CTranslate2, # so the cheapest arm installs in seconds. Heavier engines pull their own weights on # first use and the picker warns what each has cost before. python3 -c 'import piper' 2>/dev/null || pip3 install --break-system-packages -q piper-tts python3 -c 'import faster_whisper' 2>/dev/null || pip3 install --break-system-packages -q faster-whisper cd "$BENCH" || exec bash cat <<'BANNER' Everything is selected by default and a full sweep is around eleven hours. Press n to clear, then space to pick a few. piper alone takes about three minutes. BANNER # No --only: this is the interactive picker, and a terminal block is a real PTY, so # the arrow-key menu works exactly as it does on a laptop. python3 tools/benchmark.py rc=$? # No listening clips: make_samples.py exists to embed one per engine, but audio does # not reach the reader through the browser block, and it is the only reason this # needed ffmpeg -- which in turn was the only reason the sandbox ran apt-get, which # reaches deb.nodesource.com through a leftover apt source and trips egress approval. # Dropping playback drops all three. if [ -f tts-benchmark.html ]; then # page_template.html declares utf-8 upstream, so this normally just copies. The # fallback stays because the failure it guards is silent and total: python3 -m # http.server sends "text/html" with no charset, and a page that also declares # none is read as the browser's locale default, turning every em dash into # mojibake. It writes to the published copy rather than the source, so the export # zip stays byte-identical to what the tools wrote, and never doubles the tag. if grep -qi ']*charset' tts-benchmark.html; then cp -f tts-benchmark.html "$SERVE/index.html" else { printf '%s\n' ''; cat tts-benchmark.html; } > "$SERVE/index.html" fi echo "report published -> http://localhost:$PORT/" else echo "no tts-benchmark.html was produced; measurements (if any) are under $BENCH/tools/" fi echo "[tts benchmark done rc=$rc]" exec bash", "subagentIds": [], "skillIds": [], "mcpToolIds": []}
